lessons.title: From Philips Elftal to PSV
lessons.subtitle: A factory team became a wider sports association.

story.title: A workplace team
story.body: Philips employees formed the Philips Elftal in 1910, before the association PSV formally existed.

story.title: A shared beginning
story.body: The team played its first match at the site that became Philips Stadion, then joined the wider association in 1913.

facts.label: Team formed
facts.prompt: On what date did Philips employees found the Philips Elftal, PSV’s football precursor?
facts.scope: PSV’s official history dates the founding of Philips Elftal.
facts.evidence: PSV dates the founding of Philips Elftal to 12 December 1910.

facts.label: Original football team
facts.prompt: What was the name of the Philips employees’ team before it joined PSV?
facts.scope: The source names the precursor team, not the association.
facts.evidence: PSV says Philips employees founded the Philips Elftal.

facts.label: Association link
facts.prompt: When did Philips Elftal join the Philips Sport Vereniging?
facts.scope: Date the football team joined the association; it kept its own name until 1916.
facts.evidence: PSV records the team joining the association on 22 October 1913 and keeping its name until 31 October 1916.

lessons.title: A shootout crowns a golden season

story.title: A tense final
story.body: PSV and Benfica could not score in normal time or extra time in Stuttgart.

story.title: One save decides it
story.body: Hans van Breukelen stopped António Veloso’s kick as PSV won the shootout and completed a treble season.

facts.evidence: UEFA reports PSV and Benfica were 0–0 after extra time, before PSV won the shootout 6–5.

facts.scope: The Benfica player whose kick was saved in the shootout.

lessons.title: Ruud’s scoring years in Eindhoven
lessons.subtitle: From a teenage professional debut to the Eredivisie scoring crown.

story.title: An early professional start
story.body: Van Nistelrooij made his professional debut for FC Den Bosch at 17 in 1993/94. After four seasons there and one at Heerenveen, he joined PSV in 1998.

story.title: A league scoring crown
story.body: In his first PSV season, 1998/99, he scored 31 Eredivisie goals and finished as the league’s leading scorer. This total describes that league season, rather than all competitions or his entire career.

facts.label: PSV move
facts.prompt: After which club did Ruud van Nistelrooij join PSV in 1998?
facts.scope: The immediately previous club in the PSV career account.
facts.evidence: PSV says he left Heerenveen and joined PSV one year later, in 1998.

facts.label: First PSV league-season goals
facts.prompt: How many Eredivisie goals did Van Nistelrooij score in his first PSV season, 1998/99?
facts.scope: Eredivisie only, PSV, 1998/99.
facts.evidence: The Eredivisie retrospective dates his PSV arrival to 1998 and says his first-season 31 goals made him the Netherlands league top scorer.

facts.label: Professional debut age
facts.prompt: How old was Van Nistelrooij when he made his professional debut for FC Den Bosch in 1993/94?
facts.scope: Professional debut, FC Den Bosch, 1993/94.
facts.evidence: The Eredivisie retrospective explicitly gives age 17 for his professional debut under Hans van der Pluijm.

story.body: Van Nistelrooij scored all four, matching the competition’s then-record for goals by one player in a match. Liam Miller’s late cut-back set up the fourth.

facts.scope: United–Sparta Praha, 3 November 2004, added-time fourth goal.
facts.evidence: UEFA describes Miller being released on the right and cutting back for the fourth goal.
